examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > PowerPoint export
question: I have a PowerPoint with an interactive Power BI report embedded. I sent it to someone without a paid Power BI license by checking 'Show as Saved Image'. Now I want to make the report live again. What is the easiest way?
choices: Click on the add-in slide menu and select "Reload".
Click on the add-in slide menu and un-check "Show as Saved Image".
You have to redownload the Power BI report into the PowerPoint presentation.
Click on the "Data options" menu and select "Reset".
explanation: Un-checking "Show as Saved Image" in the add-in slide menu re-enables the live interactive report. The report reloads and becomes live again without needing to redownload.
choiceExplanations: "Reload" is not an option in the add-in slide menu.
Correct. Un-checking "Show as Saved Image" restores the live interactive report.
You do not need to redownload — simply un-checking the image option restores the live connection.
"Data options" and "Reset" are not the correct menu path.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > PowerPoint slicer behaviour
question: I have a Power BI report with a continent slicer. I embed it in PowerPoint with North America selected, then select Europe. I start the slide show, click Asia, then Africa. I end the slide show. What is currently selected?
choices: North America
Europe
Asia
Africa
explanation: When you end a PowerPoint slide show, all changes made during the presentation are reversed. The slicer reverts to the state it was in before the slide show started — which was Europe (selected after opening but before starting the show).
choiceExplanations: North America was the initial selection but was changed to Europe before the slide show started.
Correct. The slide show reverts to the pre-show state (Europe). Changes made during the show are discarded.
Asia was clicked during the slide show — those changes are reversed after the show ends.
Africa was the last click during the show — but slide show changes are discarded on exit.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > PowerPoint live export
question: I want Power BI to create a new PowerPoint presentation with an interactive report from the Power BI Service. I have opened the report. What do I do?
choices: Go to Export - PowerPoint - Embed live data. Then click on Copy.
Go to Export - PowerPoint - Embed an image.
Click on the ... next to a visual, then go to Share - Open in PowerPoint.
Go to Share, then click on PowerPoint, then click on "Open in PowerPoint".
explanation: To create a new PowerPoint with a live interactive Power BI report, you go to Share → PowerPoint → "Open in PowerPoint". Power BI opens PowerPoint and creates a new presentation with the live report embedded.
choiceExplanations: Export - PowerPoint - Embed live data creates a copy in the browser, not a new PowerPoint file via the app.
Embed an image creates a static image, not an interactive report.
The ... on a visual opens visual-level options, not the full report export.
Correct. Share → PowerPoint → Open in PowerPoint creates a new PowerPoint file with the live interactive report.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Share link options
question: I want to share a report. I have a Power BI Pro licence. I open the report in the Power BI Service and see the Send link dialog box. I click on the ... (More options) in the top-right corner. What is the option that I see?
choices: Allow recipients to share this report
Manage permissions
Copy link
Restrict sharing
explanation: "Manage permissions" opens a pane where you can copy links giving access, change who has Direct access, and view/modify all permissions for the report.
choiceExplanations: "Allow recipients to share this report" is a checkbox in the Send link dialog, not in the ... menu.
Correct. The ... (More options) menu shows "Manage permissions" to control all access.
"Copy link" is already visible in the main dialog, not hidden behind ...
"Restrict sharing" is not a standard Power BI option name.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Test RLS in Service
question: I want to test my dynamic Row Level Security in the Power BI Service. I go to the Row-Level Security box. I want to test the report using the MyRole security group. What do I do?
choices: Select the MyRole and click the 'Test' button.
Select the MyRole and click the 'Run report' button.
Hover over the MyRole. Select the ... to the right of MyRole and select 'Test as role'.
Select the MyRole and click the 'Save' button. Then open the report and click 'Security' at the top.
explanation: To test a role in the Power BI Service, you hover over the role name, click the ... (ellipsis) that appears, and select "Test as role". This opens the report filtered as that role would see it.
choiceExplanations: There is no standalone "Test" button next to the role.
There is no "Run report" button in the RLS panel.
Correct. Hover over the role, click ... and select "Test as role" to preview the filtered report.
Saving and clicking Security at the top of a report is not how RLS testing works.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Test RLS in Desktop
question: I want to test my dynamic Row Level Security in Power BI Desktop. I go to Modelling - View as. What role should I use?
choices: None
Other user
RLS
Custom
explanation: "Other user" lets you enter the email address of a specific user or group. This is used for dynamic RLS where the USERPRINCIPALNAME() function filters data based on the logged-in user's email.
choiceExplanations: "None" applies no RLS role, so you would see all data.
Correct. "Other user" lets you enter a role email to simulate how that user would see data with dynamic RLS.
"RLS" is not a specific role option in the View as dialog.
"Custom" is not a role option in the View as dialog.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > RLS DAX expression
question: I have created a new role. This role uses the following DAX expression for the table Customers: [PreviouslyOrdered] = TRUE(). If I use this new role, what data would I see?
choices: All customers who have previously ordered, as it filters those rows where the expression is true.
All customers who have not previously ordered, as it removes those rows where the expression is true.
All customers, regardless of whether they have previously ordered or not.
No customers — the expression excludes all rows.
explanation: An RLS DAX filter expression returns the rows where the expression evaluates to TRUE. [PreviouslyOrdered] = TRUE() filters to show only rows where the customer has previously ordered.
choiceExplanations: Correct. The RLS filter keeps rows where the expression is TRUE — customers who have previously ordered.
The filter keeps matching rows, not removes them. Rows where expression is TRUE are visible.
The filter expression limits the data — not all customers would be visible.
The expression filters TO matching rows, not away from them.
daxExpression:
-- RLS filter on Customers table: [PreviouslyOrdered] = TRUE()
-- This keeps rows where PreviouslyOrdered is TRUE
-- Users with this role only see customers who have placed an order before

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Create RLS roles
question: I want to create a new RLS role. Where do I go?
choices: In Power BI Desktop, I go to View - Roles.
In Power BI Desktop, I go to Insert - Role.
In the Power BI Service, I go to the dataset, and click on "Security".
In Power BI Desktop, I go to Modeling - Manage roles.
explanation: RLS roles are created in Power BI Desktop under Modeling - Manage roles. You can then create roles, write DAX filter expressions per table, and assign columns. Role membership is managed in the Power BI Service.
choiceExplanations: View - Roles is not a valid menu path in Power BI Desktop.
Insert - Role is not a valid menu path.
The Power BI Service is where you assign users to existing roles — not where you create them.
Correct. Modeling - Manage roles is where you create and define RLS roles in Power BI Desktop.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Data alerts
question: I want to create a data alert in a Power BI dashboard. Which of these following tiles can I NOT add a data alert on?
choices: Pie chart
Card
KPI
Gauge
explanation: Data alerts can only be set on tiles that display a single numeric value: Cards, KPIs, and Gauges. Pie charts and other complex visuals are not supported for data alerts.
choiceExplanations: Correct. Pie charts cannot have data alerts — alerts are only supported on Cards, KPIs, and Gauges.
Card tiles support data alerts.
KPI tiles support data alerts.
Gauge tiles support data alerts.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Sensitivity label settings
question: I want to create sensitivity labels but am not allowed to. The administrator enables this via Admin portal - Tenant settings - Information protection. I then need to choose who to apply it to. Which of these is NOT a valid 'apply to' setting?
choices: The entire organization
Specific security groups
Specific users
Except specific security groups
explanation: "Specific users" is not a valid target for sensitivity label permissions. You can apply to the entire organization, specific security groups, or exclude specific security groups — but not individual users.
choiceExplanations: "The entire organization" is a valid apply-to setting.
"Specific security groups" is a valid apply-to setting.
Correct. "Specific users" is not a valid option — you must use security groups or the entire organization.
"Except specific security groups" is a valid exclusion setting.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Pinned visual vs live page
question: I have a report with one table visual. I pin the table visual and pin the live page to a new dashboard. I then change the table visual to a bar chart. Which of the following is true?
choices: The pinned visual will now be a bar chart. The pinned page will include a table.
The pinned visual will still be a table. The pinned page will include a bar chart.
The pinned visual will now be a bar chart. The pinned page will include a bar chart.
The pinned visual will still be a table. The pinned page will include a table.
explanation: A pinned visual is a static snapshot — it does not update when the report changes. A pinned live page is dynamic — it reflects the current state of the report page, including any visual type changes.
choiceExplanations: A pinned visual is static and retains the original type (table). A live page reflects changes.
Correct. The pinned visual stays as a table (static snapshot); the live page updates to show the bar chart.
The pinned visual does not update — it stays as a table.
The live page does update — it would show the bar chart after the change.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Subscriptions
question: I have subscribed to a report. I want the subscription to be emailed after the data has been refreshed. What is the MAXIMUM number of times I will receive the subscription email?
choices: One email per hour.
One email per day.
One email per week.
One email per month.
explanation: When set to trigger after data refresh, the maximum frequency for a Power BI subscription email is once per day, regardless of how many times the data refreshes.
choiceExplanations: Power BI subscriptions cannot send more than once per day.
Correct. The maximum frequency for subscription emails triggered after refresh is once per day.
Once per week is below the maximum frequency — daily is the maximum.
Once per month is below the maximum frequency.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Create dashboard
question: In the Power BI Service, how do you create a dashboard?
choices: You upload it from Power BI Desktop.
You directly create it from a semantic model in the Power BI Service.
You create it from one or multiple reports or workbooks in the Power BI Service.
You create it from going to "+ Create" on the left-hand side of the Power BI Service.
explanation: Dashboards are created by pinning tiles from one or more reports or workbooks in the Power BI Service. You cannot create a dashboard by uploading from Desktop or directly from a semantic model.
choiceExplanations: Power BI Desktop publishes reports, not dashboards.
You cannot create a dashboard directly from a semantic model.
Correct. Dashboards are built by pinning visuals from reports or parts of workbooks.
"+ Create" creates reports or other items — not the primary way to create dashboards.

subtopic: Configure a semantic model scheduled refresh
examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Incremental refresh
question: I want to configure an Incremental Refresh. What two parameters do I need to create?
choices: RefreshStart and RefreshEnd
SetStart and SetEnd
PeriodStart and PeriodEnd
RangeStart and RangeEnd
explanation: Incremental Refresh requires two Power Query parameters named exactly RangeStart and RangeEnd (case-sensitive), both with DateTime data type. These are used to filter the data source during incremental loads.
choiceExplanations: RefreshStart and RefreshEnd are not the correct parameter names.
SetStart and SetEnd are not the correct parameter names.
PeriodStart and PeriodEnd are not the correct parameter names.
Correct. RangeStart and RangeEnd (case-sensitive, DateTime type) are the required parameter names.

subtopic: Configure a semantic model scheduled refresh
examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Scheduled refresh options
question: Which of these is an option when creating a Scheduled refresh for a semantic model?
choices: Send refresh success notifications to the dataset owner
Send daily notifications to the dataset owner
Send refresh failure notifications to the dataset owner
Email these users when the refresh succeeds
explanation: When configuring scheduled refresh, you can opt to send failure notifications to the dataset owner. This notifies them if the refresh fails so they can investigate and fix the issue.
choiceExplanations: Refresh success notifications are not a standard scheduled refresh option.
Daily notifications regardless of refresh status are not an option.
Correct. You can configure failure notifications to alert the dataset owner when a refresh fails.
Email on success is not a standard scheduled refresh notification option.

subtopic: Identify when a gateway is required
examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Data gateway
question: I want to refresh a semantic model which is in the Power BI Service. When would you need to use a data gateway?
choices: When you have multiple data sources in your dataset.
When at least some of your data is in your own premises network or computer.
When a semantic model is used by multiple reports.
When you want to manually update the semantic model.
explanation: A data gateway is required when your data resides on-premises (in a private network or on a local computer) and needs to be refreshed by the Power BI Service in the cloud. It acts as a secure bridge between cloud and on-premises data.
choiceExplanations: Having multiple data sources does not automatically require a gateway.
Correct. A gateway is needed when data is on your premises network or local computer — not reachable by the cloud directly.
The number of reports using a semantic model does not determine gateway requirements.
Manual refresh can be triggered from the Power BI Service without a gateway for cloud data sources.

subtopic: Promote or certify Power BI content
examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Endorsement levels
question: I want to endorse a semantic model. However, this endorsement doesn't need to be reviewed to ensure it meets my company's criteria. What endorsement does it need?
choices: Advanced
Certified
Promoted
Validated
explanation: There are two endorsement levels: Promoted (can be set by the dataset owner, no review required) and Certified (requires an admin-configured review process to confirm quality standards are met).
choiceExplanations: Advanced is not a Power BI endorsement level.
Certified requires a review process — the question says no review is needed.
Correct. Promoted endorsement can be applied by the dataset owner without a formal review.
Validated is not a Power BI endorsement level.

subtopic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Analyze in Excel
question: I go to a semantic model in the Power BI Service and click on 'Analyze in Excel'. When the Excel file opens, what do you see?
choices: A table, with the data
An empty PivotTable, so you can drag in the fields you want to show
An empty table, so you can drag in the columns you want to show
An analysis based on a report, which you can then alter
explanation: Analyze in Excel opens a connected Excel file with an empty PivotTable and the Power BI field list on the right. You then drag fields into the PivotTable to build your analysis.
choiceExplanations: The data is not pre-loaded into a flat table — you build the view yourself via PivotTable.
Correct. You get an empty PivotTable connected to the semantic model, ready for you to add fields.
PivotTable (not a flat empty table) is what appears — you drag fields, not columns.
The Excel file does not contain a pre-built analysis — it starts empty.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Publish to web
question: I want to publish my report. Which of these options is no longer available by default?
choices: Embed - Securely embed this report in a website or portal
Export to PowerPoint
Export to PDF
Publish to web - Embed this report for public access by anyone on the Internet
explanation: "Publish to web" creates a publicly accessible embed code that anyone on the internet can view. Because of security implications, it is disabled by default and must be enabled by a Power BI administrator in Tenant settings.
choiceExplanations: Secure embed is available by default for licensed users.
Export to PowerPoint is available by default.
Export to PDF is available by default.
Correct. "Publish to web" is off by default — it requires admin to enable because it makes content publicly available.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > App permissions
question: I'm looking to create an app and share it among 200 specific individuals in my organisation (which has 300 people). What is the best way to do this?
choices: You can only have 100 users in an app, so you have to create two apps.
Create an app for 100 users, and then share what reports others need.
Create a group containing these 200 people, and use this group in the permissions section.
Give access to the Entire organization, and only send the link to the 200 individuals.
explanation: The recommended approach is to create a security group with the 200 people and grant the group access in the app permissions. This is scalable and maintains proper access control.
choiceExplanations: There is no 100-user limit for apps — you can share with much larger groups.
There is no 100-user limit and this is not the recommended approach.
Correct. Create a group of 200 users and assign the group in the app permissions section.
Giving Entire organization access would include the 100 people who should not have access.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Workspace roles
question: Francis wants to access a workspace and create reports in this workspace based on existing datasets. What is the MINIMUM workspace role he needs?
choices: Admin
Member
Contributor
Viewer
explanation: Contributor role allows creating and editing content using existing datasets but not managing workspace settings or publishing apps. Member and Admin have broader permissions. Viewer can only view.
choiceExplanations: Admin has full control including managing members — more than required.
Member can publish apps and manage roles — more permissions than needed.
Correct. Contributor can create reports from existing datasets — the minimum required role.
Viewer can only view content — cannot create reports.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > App visibility
question: Brian and Chloe are working on a workspace — Brian is the Admin, Chloe is a Viewer. Brian creates an App and gives David permissions to see it. Who can view the App?
choices: David only.
Brian and David.
Brian, Chloe and David.
Brian only.
explanation: All workspace members (Brian and Chloe) automatically have access to the app because they have workspace access. David was explicitly granted permissions. So all three can view the app.
choiceExplanations: David has access, but so do workspace members Brian and Chloe.
Chloe also has access as a workspace member.
Correct. Workspace members (Brian and Chloe) automatically see apps from that workspace. David was explicitly added.
Brian is the only one mentioned here but Chloe and David also have access.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > App limits
question: What is the maximum number of dashboards allowed in an App?
choices: Zero - they are not allowed in an App.
explanation: An app can contain up to 200 dashboards in addition to reports and other content.
choiceExplanations: Dashboards are allowed in apps.
1 dashboard would be too restrictive — the limit is 200.
20 is not the correct limit.
Correct. An app can include up to 200 dashboards.

subtopic: Create a narrative visual with Copilot
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Copilot features
question: I want to use Copilot to summarize the underlying semantic model. Where do I need to ask that question?
choices: Semantic model
Report
Dashboard
Power BI Desktop
explanation: Copilot for summarizing the underlying semantic model is accessed from within a Report in the Power BI Service — not directly from the semantic model view or a dashboard.
choiceExplanations: Copilot for semantic model summarization is accessed from a Report, not the semantic model itself.
Correct. Copilot to summarize the semantic model is available within Reports in the Power BI Service.
Copilot is not available from Dashboard tiles.
Power BI Desktop does not have Copilot for semantic model summarization.

subtopic: Create a narrative visual with Copilot
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Narrative visual
question: Which of the following visuals uses Copilot?
choices: Narrative
Key influencers
Decomposition tree
KPI
explanation: The Narrative visual uses Copilot to automatically generate text summaries and insights about the data in your report. Key influencers and Decomposition tree are AI visuals but do not use Copilot.
choiceExplanations: Correct. The Narrative visual leverages Copilot to generate natural language summaries of the data.
Key influencers is an AI visual but uses machine learning, not Copilot.
Decomposition tree is an AI visual for hierarchical exploration — not Copilot powered.
KPI is a standard visual, not powered by Copilot.

subtopic: Use Copilot to create a new report page
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Copilot availability
question: In which of the following places on the Power BI Service can you use Copilot?
choices: Semantic models
Reports
Dashboards
You can't - you can only use it in Power BI Desktop.
explanation: Copilot in the Power BI Service is available in Reports — you can use it to create report pages, summarize data, and generate insights. It is not available directly in the semantic model view or on dashboards.
choiceExplanations: Copilot is not available directly in the semantic model view.
Correct. Copilot is available in Reports within the Power BI Service.
Copilot is not available in the Dashboard view.
Copilot is available in the Power BI Service (Reports), not just Desktop.

subtopic: Use Copilot to create a new report page
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Copilot Fabric capacity
question: I want to use Copilot in the Power BI Service. What is the minimum Fabric capacity that I need to have in the relevant workspace?
choices: F1
F2
You don't need a Fabric capacity.
explanation: Copilot in the Power BI Service requires a minimum of F2 Fabric capacity in the workspace. F1 is not sufficient for Copilot features.
choiceExplanations: F1 capacity is not sufficient for Copilot — the minimum is F2.
Correct. Copilot in the Power BI Service requires at least F2 Fabric capacity.
F64 would work but is far more than the minimum required.
A Fabric capacity (minimum F2) is required for Copilot in the Power BI Service.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Get or connect to data
commonTrap: Confusing 'Get Data' with 'Load Data'
question: I want to add a new data source into my existing Power BI file. What option do I need to go to?
choices: Load Data
Get Data
Open Data
Find Data
explanation: In Power BI Desktop, 'Get Data' is the entry point for connecting to any data source. It is found on the Home tab.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Create reports
commonTrap: Confusing Focus mode with Zoom mode
question: When I have selected a visual, I can click on an icon that magnifies the visual (shows it bigger, without any other visuals showing). What is this icon called?
choices: Data mode
Focus mode
Zoom mode
Expand
explanation: Focus mode enlarges a single visual to fill the entire canvas. You can exit Focus mode by clicking 'Back to report'.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Create reports
commonTrap: Thinking the visual must be deselected first
question: I have added a table visual to my existing Power BI file. I want to change it to a stacked bar chart. What is one way of doing this?
choices: Ensure that no visual is selected, then go to Home - Insert - Stacked bar chart.
Ensure that no visual is selected, go to the Data/Fields pane, click on the fields, and select 'stacked bar chart'.
Ensure the visual is selected, and go to 'Build a Visual'/Visualization pane, and click on 'stacked bar chart'.
Ensure the visual is selected, and go to Data/Fields pane, and click on 'stacked bar chart'.
explanation: To change a visual type, the visual must be selected. You then go to the Visualization pane (Build a Visual) and click the desired chart type.

subtopic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Publish, import, or update items in a workspace
commonTrap: Thinking 'Share' or 'Upload' is the correct menu option
question: I want to add my existing report to the Power BI Service. What option do I go to?
choices: File - Publish - Publish to Power BI
File - Upload - Upload to Power BI
File - Share - Share to Power BI
File - Move - Move to Power BI
explanation: To publish a report from Power BI Desktop to the Power BI Service, go to File > Publish > Publish to Power BI. You can also use the Publish button on the Home tab.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data > Select appropriate column data types
commonTrap: Assuming Image is a valid data type because Binary is
question: Which of the following is NOT a valid data type for a field in Power BI?
choices: Whole number
Image
Date/time
Text
explanation: Image is not a valid data type in Power BI. Valid types include Whole number, Decimal number, Fixed decimal number, Date/time, Date, Time, Text, True/False, and Binary.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Going to the Data pane or Format pane instead of the Visualization pane
question: I have created a visual which includes 'Sum of SalesVolume'. I wish to change the aggregation from Sum to Average for this visual only. How can I do this?
choices: Click on the field in the Data pane, and go to Column tools.
Select the visual, and go to the 'Build a visual'/Visualization pane.
Select the visual, and right-hand click on the visualization.
Select the visual, and go to the Format pane.
explanation: To change the aggregation for a specific visual, select the visual and go to the Build a Visual/Visualization pane. You can then right-click on the field or click the arrow next to it to change the aggregation.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Looking for a 'Copy Formatting' right-click option
question: I have two visuals. I have fully formatted the first visual. I wish to copy the formatting from the first visual to the second. How can I do this?
choices: Click on the first visual, select Home - Format Painter, and click on the second visual.
Click on the first visual, select Home - Format Special - Formats, and click on the second visual.
Click on the first visual, select Home - Copy, click on the second visual, and select Paste - Formats.
Right-hand click on the first visual, select Copy - Copy Formatting, and click on the second visual.
explanation: Format Painter in the Home tab allows you to copy formatting from one visual and apply it to another by clicking the target visual.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Create reports
commonTrap: Using double-click or right-click instead of Ctrl+click
question: I want to select two visuals at the same time. I click on the first visual. How do I select the second visual?
choices: Double-click on the second visual
Right-hand click on this second visual
Hold down Control and click on the second visual
Hold down Alt and click on the second visual
explanation: Hold down Ctrl (Control) and click on the second visual to select both visuals simultaneously. You can also use Shift+click to select both visuals.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Select an appropriate visual
commonTrap: Thinking Line and clustered bar chart is a standard single visual
question: Which of these is a standard visual which you can select in the 'Build a visual'/Visualization pane? Note - this is a single visual, not two different visuals.
choices: Line and clustered bar chart
Line and pie chart
Line chart and table
Line and stacked column chart
explanation: The 'Line and stacked column chart' is a standard combined visual in Power BI. You can also use a 'Line and clustered column chart'. There is no built-in 'Line and pie chart' or 'Line chart and table' combined visual.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Select an appropriate visual
commonTrap: Confusing stacked column chart with clustered column chart
question: A visual shows years 2000-2016 along the X-axis, Sales Volume on the Y-axis, and a series of bars in different colors for each region stacked on top of each other per year. What type of visual is this?
choices: Clustered column chart
Stacked column chart
Clustered bar chart
Stacked bar chart
explanation: A stacked column chart shows vertical bars with segments stacked on top of each other, each segment representing a category (e.g., region). A clustered column chart would show separate bars side by side.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure drillthrough navigation
commonTrap: Thinking only the selected year expands, not all years
question: I have a matrix which has the OrderDate hierarchy in the rows section. It is currently showing the Years 2023 to 2025. What happens if I click on the year 2024, then click on 'Expand all down one level in the hierarchy'?
choices: All of the years in the OrderDate field will be expanded to the Year and Month hierarchy.
All of the years in the OrderDate field will be expanded to the Year and Quarter hierarchy.
The 2024 year only will be expanded into months. The other years will remain as years.
Instead of showing OrderDate years, it will show Quarters instead.
explanation: 'Expand all down one level' expands ALL rows down one level in the hierarchy — not just the selected row. In a standard date hierarchy, below Year is Quarter, so all years expand to show quarters.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Select an appropriate visual
commonTrap: Thinking both table and matrix can summarise data
question: What is the difference between a table and a matrix in Power BI?
choices: A table can summarise data. A matrix cannot summarise data.
A table cannot summarise data. A matrix can summarise data.
A table has a fixed number of columns. A matrix has a variable number of columns.
A table has a variable number of columns. A matrix has a fixed number of columns.
explanation: A table has a fixed column for each field in the columns area. A matrix has a column for the rows area, plus columns for each unique value in the column fields — making its number of columns variable.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure sync slicers
commonTrap: Confusing Sync Slicers with Edit Interactions
question: What does Sync Slicers do?
choices: It allows a single slicer to affect multiple pages.
It allows you to choose which visuals on the same page are affected by the slicer.
It allows you to format the style of the slicer.
explanation: Sync Slicers (View > Sync Slicers) allows a slicer on one page to filter visuals on other pages. You can also control whether the slicer is visible on those other pages.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Apply slicing and filtering
commonTrap: Thinking slicer affects all pages by default
question: I have just created a slicer on a page which has 3 other visuals. By default, what visuals does this slicer affect?
choices: The nearest visual to the slicer.
The visuals that you choose in the Format pane.
All visuals on that page.
All visuals in the report (all pages).
explanation: By default, a slicer affects all visuals on the same page. To extend it to other pages, you use View - Sync Slicers.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Apply slicing and filtering
commonTrap: Confusing ? with * or % wildcard characters
question: I want to create an Advanced Filter. Which of these is a wildcard I can use which represents exactly one character?
explanation: In Advanced Filters, '?' represents exactly one character, and '*' represents zero, one or multiple characters.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Apply slicing and filtering
commonTrap: Using Basic filtering when conditions like 'contains' are needed
question: I go to View - Filters and can see 'Filters on this visual', 'Filters on this page' and 'Filters on all pages'. I want to add a filter that shows only those Region Names which contain 'East' or 'Midlands', and the filter should automatically update when data changes. Which Filter Type should I use?
choices: Basic filtering
Advanced filtering
Top N
Relative date
explanation: Advanced filtering allows conditions such as 'contains', 'greater than', and 'is not blank'. Basic filtering only provides checkboxes for specific values.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Group and layer visuals by using the Selection pane
commonTrap: Going to Format pane instead of Selection pane
question: I want to hide a visual. Which pane do I go to?
choices: The Format pane
The Bookmarks pane
The Sync Slicers pane
The Selection pane
explanation: The Selection pane (View > Selection) allows you to hide visuals, change their layer order, and manage tab order for accessibility.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure bookmarks
commonTrap: Thinking bookmarks save the data source
question: Which of the following do bookmarks NOT do?
choices: Save data sources
Save filter, drill and sort state
Save visual display state
Save the current page
explanation: Bookmarks capture the state of a report page including filters, visuals, slicers, and page visibility — but they do NOT save data sources.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Putting the field in Legend instead of Small multiples
question: I want to change a stacked bar chart visual so that, instead of showing one bar chart, it shows many charts, one for each Department. Where do I put the Department field?
choices: In the Y-axis area
In the Legend area
In the Small multiples area
In the Tooltips area
explanation: Dragging a field into the Small multiples area creates a separate chart for each value of that field. Legend would color-code within a single chart.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Apply sorting to visuals
commonTrap: Looking for a dedicated Sort button or going to View menu
question: I want to sort data descending in a visual. What do I do to achieve this?
choices: Click on the ↓ down arrow next to a visual.
Click on the ... next to a visual
Go to View - Sort.
Go to the Format pane.
explanation: To sort a visual, click on the '...' (more options) icon next to the visual, then go to Sort by to change the sort field and direction.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure navigation for a report
commonTrap: Looking in Insert - Shapes instead of Insert - Buttons
question: Where can you add a bookmark navigator?
choices: In the Home menu - you can insert it like any visual.
In the Insert menu - Buttons
In the Insert menu - Shapes
In the Modeling menu
explanation: A bookmark navigator is found under Insert > Buttons. It creates a button group that navigates between bookmarks.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure navigation for a report
commonTrap: Thinking Text Boxes support Action types like Buttons do
question: Using the 'on-object interaction' feature, which of the following ways can I NOT insert something that will allow the user to run a Q&A?
choices: Go to the Home menu and, in the Insert drop-down box, under AI visuals, click on Q&A.
Go to Insert and add a Text Box. In the Format pane for the Text Box, change the 'Action' to Q&A.
Go to Insert menu and click on Q&A.
Go to Insert and click on Buttons, and then click on Q&A.
explanation: Text Boxes do not have an 'Action' option in their Format pane. Only Buttons, Shapes, and Images support Actions. Therefore, a Text Box cannot be configured to launch Q&A.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure navigation for a report
commonTrap: Thinking Sync Slicers is a button action
question: Which of these is NOT a valid Action for a Button?
choices: Back
Bookmark
Q&A
Sync slicers
explanation: Valid Actions for buttons include: Back, Bookmark, Drill through, Page navigation, Q&A, and Web URL. Sync Slicers is a View menu feature, not a button action.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure drillthrough navigation
commonTrap: Confusing drill-through with drill-down within a visual
question: What is an example of what a drill-through does?
choices: In a visual, the X-axis can change from Years to Quarters.
You can go from a summary page to a detailed page.
In a visual, the X-axis can change from Years to Years and Quarters.
In a visual, the X-axis can change from showing all years to focusing on one particular year and showing Quarters.
explanation: Drill-through navigates from one report page to another (e.g., summary to detail). Drill-down changes hierarchy levels within the same visual.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Putting SalesVolume into the Y Axis instead of Size
question: I am creating a scatter chart. I want to change it into a bubble chart so that the bubble is bigger when SalesVolume is higher, and smaller when SalesVolume is lower. Where do I need to drag the SalesVolume field?
choices: Into the Size section.
Into the Area section.
Into the Y Axis.
Into the Legend.
explanation: In a scatter/bubble chart, the Size field controls the size of each bubble. Placing SalesVolume in Size means higher values produce larger bubbles.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Putting Year in the Time Axis instead of Play Axis
question: I want to animate a scatter chart, showing the result for individual years. Where do I need to put the Year field?
choices: In the Time Axis.
In the Play Axis.
In the Breakdown Axis.
In the Legend.
explanation: The Play Axis in a scatter chart enables animation. When a field is placed in the Play Axis, you can click the Play button to animate the chart across each value (e.g., year).

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Going to Format pane to deselect Cumulative Total instead of using Breakdown
question: I am creating a waterfall chart. It is currently showing a cumulative total. I want it to show each category individually, not cumulatively. What do I need to do?
choices: Add a field to the Category area.
Add a field to the Y-axis area.
Add a field to the Breakdown area.
Go to the Format pane, to the Totals section, and deselect 'Cumulative Total'.
explanation: In a waterfall chart, adding a field to the Breakdown area shows each category separately rather than as a running cumulative total.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Create reports
commonTrap: Confusing AppSource with PowerBI.com marketplace
question: What is the name of the marketplace where you download custom Power BI visuals?
choices: PowerBICenter
AppSource
VisualStudio
AnalysisStore
explanation: Custom Power BI visuals are downloaded from Microsoft AppSource. You can access it directly from the Visualization pane in Power BI Desktop.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Select an appropriate visual
commonTrap: Confusing conversion rate with completion rate
question: A funnel chart shows that 100% of users start the first process, but only 71.5% complete the last process. What is this percentage called?
choices: The conversion rate
The success rate
The completion rate
The checkout rate
explanation: The conversion rate in a funnel chart represents the percentage of users who complete the entire process from start to finish.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Thinking the Category and Details sections behave identically for color assignment
question: I am creating a treemap with RegionName in the Category section. I want to add Year into either the Category or the Details section. Which of the following statements is true about the color behavior?
choices: If Year is in either section, all rectangles for a particular RegionName will be different colors.
If Year is in either section, all rectangles for a particular RegionName will be the same color.
If Year is in the Category section, rectangles for the same RegionName will be the same color. If Year is in the Details section, they will be different colors.
If Year is in the Category section, rectangles for the same RegionName will be different colors. If Year is in the Details section, they will be the same color.
explanation: In a treemap, fields in the Category section define color groupings. Adding Year to Category makes each Year a separate color group. Fields in the Details section break categories into sub-rectangles but share the parent category color.

subtopic: Design and implement a data model
examObjective: Model the data > Configure table and column properties
commonTrap: Looking in Report view Field pane or Modeling menu
question: I have created a hierarchy of Country - City - State. I realise it is in the wrong order. I need to move 'City' down. Where do I go to do that?
choices: In the Report view, I go to the Field pane.
In the Report view, I go to the Modeling menu.
In the Data view, I go to the Data pane.
In the Model view, I click on the table and go to the Properties pane.
explanation: To reorder levels in a hierarchy, go to Model view, click on the table containing the hierarchy, find it in the Properties pane, and drag the levels to reorder them. Click 'Apply Level Changes' to confirm.

subtopic: Design and implement a data model
examObjective: Model the data > Configure table and column properties
commonTrap: Using Data type instead of Data category for geographic fields
question: In Power BI Desktop, which Column tools dropdown allows you to specify that a field relates to a geographic concept such as a country, county, state or province, postal code, or address?
choices: Summarization
Data type
Data category
Geographical location
explanation: The Data category property in Column tools lets you classify a field as a geographic concept (Country, State, City, Postal code, etc.), which helps Power BI map visuals accurately.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Select an appropriate visual
commonTrap: Confusing heat map with bubble map
question: A map shows various location circles with a light red outside and a dark red inside. Some circles combine to form bigger, darker areas. What is this type of map called in Power BI?
choices: Bubble map
Heat map
Filled map
ArcGIS
explanation: A heat map shows data density or intensity through color gradients. Overlapping circles that combine into darker areas is the heat map visual behavior in Power BI.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Thinking 'Find' is a standard map control option
question: I can add or remove map controls by going to the Format pane, then Map settings - Controls. Which of the following is NOT a control I can add or remove?
choices: Auto zoom
Navigation
Selection
Find
explanation: Available map controls include Auto zoom, Navigation, and Selection (lasso). 'Find' is not available — you cannot add a button to search for locations in the map visual.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Select an appropriate visual
commonTrap: Thinking Breakdown is part of a KPI (it is used in waterfall charts)
question: Which of the following is NOT included in a KPI visual?
choices: Icons
Trend axis
Breakdown
Callout value
explanation: KPI visuals include a Callout value (the main metric), Trend axis (shows progress over time), and Goal/Target. 'Breakdown' is a field used in waterfall charts, not KPIs.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Apply conditional formatting
commonTrap: Choosing 'Field value' when no color column exists
question: I have a table showing quarterly data. I want to apply conditional formatting background colors: Spring = Green, Summer = Yellow, Autumn/Fall = Brown, Winter = White. I do not have a separate color column — the colors must come from the Quarter field itself. What Format style should I use?
choices: Gradient
Rules
Field value
Data bar
explanation: Rules-based conditional formatting lets you define specific conditions (e.g., if field equals 'Spring', apply Green). 'Field value' would require a column that already stores color values. 'Gradient' works with numeric ranges.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Select an appropriate visual
commonTrap: Thinking a Card shows a bar chart or icons
question: Apart from the measure name, which of the following is shown in a Card visual?
choices: An area chart
Icons
A number
A bar chart
explanation: A Card visual displays a single number (a measure value) along with the measure name. You can also show the First or Last value of a text field.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Turning off Data labels instead of Callout value
question: I have a gauge visual that shows '88.14K' in the middle of the gauge. I want to remove this figure. I click on the gauge and go to the Format pane. What should I turn off?
choices: Data labels
Target label
Callout value
Title
explanation: The Callout value in a gauge visual is the large number displayed in the center of the gauge arc. Turning it off removes this number from the visual.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Use reference lines, error bars, and forecasting
commonTrap: Thinking 'By formula' is a valid error bar type
question: I want to add an error bar to my line chart. After enabling Error bars in the Format pane, I go to the 'Type' dropdown. Which of these is NOT a possible option?
choices: By field
By percentage
By formula
By percentile
explanation: Error bar types in Power BI include: By field, By percentage, By percentile, and By standard deviation. 'By formula' is not a valid option.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure export settings
commonTrap: Thinking all columns in the dataset are exported
question: I have a dataset with columns: Year, Month, Sick Leave Hours, and Vacation Hours. My clustered column chart shows Sick Leave Hours by Month. I click '...' on the visual and select 'Export Data'. How many columns does this exported data have?
choices: 1 (Sick Leave Hours)
2 (Month and Sick Leave Hours)
3 (Year, Month and Sick Leave Hours)
4 (Year, Month, Sick Leave Hours and Vacation Hours)
explanation: Exporting data from a visual exports only the data that makes up that visual. Since the chart shows Sick Leave Hours by Month, only those two columns are exported.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure export settings
commonTrap: Thinking it exports as Excel
question: I click on the '...' to the top-right of a clustered column chart visual and click 'Export Data'. What format does it export as?
choices: Excel workbook
PDF document
PowerPoint presentation
Comma Separated Values (CSV) file
explanation: Exporting visual data from a Power BI Desktop report downloads a CSV file. You can then import it into Excel or other tools.

subtopic: Create model calculations by using DAX
examObjective: Model the data > Create model calculations by using DAX > Create a measure by using quick measures
commonTrap: Using the Date Hierarchy level instead of the base date field
question: I want to create a Quick Measure that calculates the year-to-date total of SalesVolume based on the OrderDate field. The OrderDate has a hierarchy with Year, Quarter, Month, and Day. After selecting 'Year-to-date total', what fields should I add and where?
choices: Base value = OrderDate / Date = SalesVolume
Base value = SalesVolume / Date = OrderDate - Date Hierarchy - Day
Base value = SalesVolume / Date = OrderDate - Date Hierarchy - Year
Base value = SalesVolume / Date = OrderDate
explanation: For a YTD Quick Measure, 'Base value' is the measure to total (SalesVolume), and 'Date' should be the date field itself (OrderDate), not a hierarchy level. The hierarchy levels are not date fields.
daxExpression:
-- Quick Measure: Year-to-date total of SalesVolume based on OrderDate
-- Power BI generates this DAX automatically:
SalesVolume YTD =
    TOTALYTD(
        SUM('Table'[SalesVolume]),
        'Table'[OrderDate]
    )

-- In the Quick Measure wizard:
--   Calculation: Year-to-date total
--   Base value: SalesVolume
--   Date: OrderDate

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Create a narrative visual with Copilot
commonTrap: Right-clicking and selecting 'Smart Narrative' instead of 'Summarize'
question: I have a page with just one visual and want to create a Smart Narrative. Besides going to Home or Insert to add the visual, what other way can I create one?
choices: Click on the ... next to the visual, and go to Smart Narrative.
Click on the ... next to the visual, and go to Summarize.
Right-hand click on the visual, and go to Smart Narrative.
Right-hand click on the visual, and go to Summarize.
explanation: Right-clicking on a visual and selecting 'Summarize' creates a Smart Narrative visual linked to that visual. The '...' menu does not contain a Smart Narrative or Summarize option.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Use grouping, binning, and clustering
commonTrap: Thinking 'Include Other group' is available for Bin type
question: I create a group by right-clicking a field and selecting 'New group'. The Groups dialog box appears. Which of the following statements is true about the Groups dialog box?
choices: When 'Group type' is 'Bin', it divides numerical values into similarly-sized ranges.
When 'Group type' is 'Bin', I can check 'Include Other group'.
'Group type' is 'List' is primarily used for fields which contain numerical values.
For fields which contain text values, you can choose either 'Group type' to be 'List' or 'Bin'.
explanation: Bin groups divide numerical values into equally-sized ranges. You can then set 'Bin size' or 'Number of bins'. 'Include Other group' is only available for List type, and Bin type requires numerical fields.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Detect outliers and anomalies
commonTrap: Thinking higher sensitivity means fewer anomalies
question: I have a line chart with 'Find anomalies' turned on. Sensitivity is at 50% and 10 points are currently highlighted as anomalous. If I change sensitivity to 80%, which outcome is most likely?
choices: The number of anomalous points will go down to 9 or less.
The number of anomalous points will remain at 10, as sensitivity does not affect this.
The number of anomalous points will go up to 11 or more.
You cannot change the sensitivity directly — you must change the Expected Range instead.
explanation: Higher sensitivity means the 'normal' band becomes narrower, so more data points fall outside it and are flagged as anomalous. Increasing sensitivity from 50% to 80% will likely increase the number of anomalous points.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Use grouping, binning, and clustering
commonTrap: Right-clicking on a field in the Data pane instead of using the visual menu
question: I have a scatter chart and want to ask Power BI to 'automatically find clusters' and divide the plots into 5 clusters. Where do I go to do this?
choices: Right-hand click on the date field in the Values section in the Build a Visual pane.
Right-hand click on the SalesVolume field in the Data pane.
Click on the ... in the top-right hand corner of the visual.
Right-hand click anywhere on the scatter chart.
explanation: Automatic cluster detection for a scatter chart is accessed via the '...' (more options) menu in the top-right corner of the visual. From there, select 'Automatically find clusters'.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Select an appropriate visual
commonTrap: Using a line or stacked column chart for outlier detection
question: Which visualization technique is best suited for identifying outliers in a dataset of employee expenses?
choices: Using a Stacked column chart, with Year and Month in the X-axis, and Expense in the Y-axis.
Using a Line chart, with Year and Month in the X-axis, and Expense in the Y-axis.
Using a Scatter chart, with the Date Hierarchy in the X-axis, Expense in the Y-axis, and Person ID in the Legend.
Using a Pie chart, with the Date Hierarchy in the Legend, and Expense in the Values.
explanation: A scatter chart with Person ID in the Legend shows individual data points per person, making it easy to identify outliers. The Date Hierarchy in the X-axis allows drilling into specific time periods.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Choose when to use a paginated report
commonTrap: Thinking Excel can be used as a data source in Report Builder
question: I want to create a paginated report. Which of the following data sources can I NOT connect to in Power BI Report Builder?
choices: Microsoft Azure SQL Database
Microsoft Excel
Microsoft SQL Server Analysis Services
Oracle Database
explanation: Power BI Report Builder (for paginated reports) connects to online database sources like Azure SQL, SQL Server Analysis Services, and Oracle. Microsoft Excel is not supported as a data source.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Use the Analyze feature in Power BI
commonTrap: Right-clicking on the high bar (2007) instead of the low bar (2008)
question: I have a bar chart showing Year on the X-axis and Sales Volume on the Y-axis. Sales is high in 2007 and low in 2008. I want Power BI to explain why there is this difference. What should I do?
choices: Right-hand click the bar in 2007 and select Analyze - Explain the decrease.
Right-hand click the visual and select Summarize.
Right-hand click the bar in 2008 and select Analyze - Explain the decrease.
Right-hand click the visual and select Explain the distribution.
explanation: To explain a decrease, right-click on the lower value (2008 bar) and select Analyze > Explain the decrease. Power BI will identify factors contributing to the drop from 2007 to 2008.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Use AI visuals
commonTrap: Confusing Expand by (Key Influencers) with Decomposition Tree sections
question: Which of the following sections is NOT used in the AI Decomposition Tree visual?
choices: Analyze
Explain by
Expand by
explanation: 'Expand by' is used in the Key Influencers visual to show what a metric expands to. The Decomposition Tree uses 'Analyze' (the metric) and 'Explain by' (the dimensions to break down by).

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Use AI visuals
commonTrap: Dragging Region Name into Analyze or Expand by
question: I have a Key Influencers visual that shows the effect of year and month on Sales Volume. I also want to see the effect of Region Name on Sales Volume. What should I do?
choices: Drag 'Region Name' into the Analyze section.
Drag 'Region Name' into the 'Explain by' section.
Drag 'Region Name' into the 'Expand by' section.
Remove Date from 'Explain by' first, then drag 'Region Name' into the 'Explain by' section.
explanation: In Key Influencers, the 'Explain by' section contains the dimensions that may influence the metric. You can add multiple fields; removing existing fields is not required.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data
commonTrap: Thinking Remove Range of Rows is available like Keep Range of Rows
question: Which of these is NOT an option when looking at Home - Remove Rows in Power Query Editor?
choices: Remove Top Rows
Remove Bottom Rows
Remove Range of Rows
Remove Blank Rows
explanation: In Power Query, you can use Home > Keep Rows > Keep Range of Rows, but there is no 'Remove Range of Rows' option. You can Remove Top Rows, Remove Bottom Rows, Remove Duplicates, Remove Blank Rows, and Remove Errors.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data
commonTrap: Thinking 'Go to Column' removes the column
question: In the Power Query Editor, I want to remove a column called Comments. Which of the following options could NOT, by itself, remove the column?
choices: In the Home tab, click on Choose Columns - Choose Columns
In the Home tab, click on Choose Columns - Go to Column
In the Home tab, click on Remove Columns - Remove Column
In the Home tab, click on Remove Columns - Remove Other Columns
explanation: 'Go to Column' simply highlights/scrolls to a column — it does not remove it. 'Choose Columns' lets you select which columns to keep (deselecting Comments removes it). 'Remove Column' and 'Remove Other Columns' can also remove it.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data > Identify when to use reference or duplicate queries
commonTrap: Thinking Duplicate and Reference behave the same way
question: What is the difference between Duplicating a query and Referencing it?
choices: Duplicating a query copies the current query. Referencing a query only copies the location of its data source.
Duplicating a query copies the current query. Referencing a query creates a link to the query, so if the original changes, the reference is updated.
Referencing a query copies the current query. Duplicating a query only copies the location of its data source.
Referencing a query copies the current query. Duplicating a query creates a link, so if the original changes, the duplicate is updated.
explanation: Duplicate creates an independent copy — changes to the original don't affect the duplicate. Reference creates a dependent link — if the original query changes, the referenced query reflects those changes.

tables.name: Duplicate vs Reference behaviour
rows: A copy of all steps evaluated from source
Independent — changes to original do NOT affect duplicate
A new query pointing to the output of original
Dependent — original runs first; reference sees its final output

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data
commonTrap: Using underscore or dash notation instead of dot notation
question: The Power Query Editor uses a language called 'M'. When you add an applied step, it is translated into M formulas. Which of the following is in the correct format to be an M function?
choices: Text-Proper
Text_Proper
TextProper
Text.Proper
explanation: M functions use dot notation with two parts separated by a dot (e.g., Text.Proper, Text.Upper, Date.Year). All words start with a capital letter and there are no spaces.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data > Select appropriate column data types
commonTrap: Thinking the 'any' type shows only ABC or only 123
question: I have imported some data. In one column, Power Query Editor cannot determine what data type it should be. What does the symbol for the default or 'any' data type contain?
choices: ABC
A globe
ABC / 123
explanation: The 'any' or unknown data type is represented by the symbol showing both 'ABC' and '123' together, indicating the column could contain any type of data.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data
commonTrap: Thinking 'By Word' is a valid split option (it isn't — use 'By Delimiter' with space instead)
question: I want to split a text field. I go to Home - Split Column. Which of the following is NOT a valid option?
choices: By Number of Characters
By Positions
By Word
By Lowercase to Uppercase
explanation: Split Column options include: By Delimiter, By Number of Characters, By Positions, By Lowercase to Uppercase, By Uppercase to Lowercase, and By Digit to Non-Digit. 'By Word' is not valid — use 'By Delimiter' with a space character instead.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data
commonTrap: Clicking on the filter drop-down instead of deleting the Applied Step
question: I have an Employee dataset in Power Query Editor. I filtered the Town column to show only Boston employees, then sorted by Last Name ascending. I now want to re-filter to show only New York employees. What is the easiest way?
choices: Click on the filter next to Town. Unselect Boston and select New York.
Delete the last Applied Step. Click on the filter next to Town and select New York.
Delete the current query. Reload the data. Click on the filter next to Town and select New York.
Close and Apply. In Power BI Desktop Data view, click the filter next to Town and select New York.
explanation: The last Applied Step is the sort step. Deleting it makes the filter step the current step, which you can then edit to change the filter value to New York. You could also delete both steps if needed.

rows: Filtered Rows — Town = Boston  ← needs to become New York
Sorted Rows — Last Name ascending  ← must be deleted first

rows: Delete step 4 (sort) — it must be re-applied after the filter changes
Click the filter arrow on Town in step 3 → uncheck Boston → check New York
Re-apply sort on Last Name if needed

examObjective: Prepare the data > Get or connect to data
commonTrap: Using Merge Files or Append Files instead of Combine Files
question: I have 20 files of the same format in a Windows folder. How can I easily get the data from all of these files in one query?
choices: Go to Home - Merge Files
Go to Home - Append Files
Go to Home - Combine Files
Go to Home - Load Files
explanation: In Power Query, Home > Combine Files lets you combine multiple files from a folder into a single query. You connect to the folder first, then use Combine Files to merge all files of the same format.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data > Merge and append queries
commonTrap: Thinking appended queries lose columns that don't match, or error on type mismatch
question: Query1 has columns: Date, Subject, Comments (Subject is text). Query2 has columns: Date, Cost, Comments (Cost is decimal). I append these queries into a new query. How many columns does the new query have?
choices: 3: Date, Subject and Comments.
4: Date, Subject, Comments and Cost.
6: Date, Subject, Comments, Date, Cost and Comments.
This results in an error, as the second column has two different data types.
explanation: Appending queries stacks rows and creates a union of all columns. Unique columns from each query are added — Date and Comments overlap, while Subject and Cost are unique. Null values fill where a column doesn't exist in one query.

expectedOutput.label: After Append — 4 columns (union of both schemas), nulls where column absent

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data > Merge and append queries
commonTrap: Right-clicking the header or clicking the table icon instead of the expand icon
question: I have merged a 'CD Categorisation' query (with Path and CD Type columns) into a 'CDs' query. The merged column shows 'Table' for each row. I want to see the CD Type column for all rows. What should I do?
choices: Click on the Table icon in the top-left hand corner.
Right-hand click on the 'CD Categorisation' header and select 'Expand'.
Click on the icon in the top-right hand corner of the column header which has two arrows, one pointing left and one pointing right.
Click on the word 'Table' in the data section.
explanation: After a merge, the nested table column shows a double-arrow expand icon in the top-right of the column header. Clicking it lets you select which columns from the merged table to expand into the main query.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data > Merge and append queries
commonTrap: Thinking you can merge three queries simultaneously
question: Which of these statements about merging queries is NOT correct?
choices: I can merge three queries together at the same time.
I can append three queries together at the same time.
I can combine three files together at the same time.
explanation: Merge Queries can only merge two queries at a time. To merge three queries, you must merge two first, then merge the result with the third. Append and Combine Files both support multiple sources at once.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data > Merge and append queries
commonTrap: Confusing Left Outer with Inner join
question: In Power Query Editor, I merge Query1 with Query2 (Query1 on top). The Join Kind defaults to 'Left Outer'. What does a Left Outer join retrieve?
choices: It retrieves all rows from both Query1 and Query2.
It retrieves only the rows from Query1 and Query2 that match.
It retrieves all rows from Query2, and those rows in Query1 that match.
It retrieves all rows from Query1, and those rows in Query2 that match.
explanation: Left Outer join returns all rows from the left (first) table — Query1 — and only matching rows from the right table — Query2. Non-matching rows from Query2 are excluded; non-matching Query1 rows get null values.

expectedOutput.label: Left Outer Join result — all Query1 rows, null where no Query2 match

question: I am going to use Transform - Unpivot. It will remove several columns and create two new columns. What are those two new columns called?
choices: Heading and Total
Attribute and Value
Column A and Column B
Key and Data
explanation: Transform > Unpivot Columns creates two new columns: 'Attribute' (the headers of the removed columns) and 'Value' (the data values that were in those columns).

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data > Pivot, unpivot, and transpose data
commonTrap: Not removing unnecessary columns before pivoting
question: My dataset has columns: Date, Region, Area, AreaCode, SalesVolume. Regions are Northeast, Midwest, South, West. I want to pivot so that Date goes down and each Region becomes a separate column summing SalesVolume (5 total columns). What must I do BEFORE using Transform - Pivot Column?
choices: Remove Area and AreaCode columns.
Move the SalesVolume column next to the Region column.
Nothing — you can select which columns to show after pivoting.
Highlight the Date, Region and SalesVolume columns.
explanation: Before pivoting, the dataset should only contain the columns you want to use in the pivot. All other columns (Area, AreaCode) must be removed first, otherwise Power Query tries to aggregate them and the result will not be what you expect.

commonTrap: Selecting 'Date' as the Values Column instead of 'SalesVolume'
question: My dataset has columns: Date, Region, SalesVolume. Regions are Northeast, Midwest, South, West. I want Date down the left side and each Region as a column with the sum of SalesVolume (5 total columns). How do I do this?
choices: Go to the Region column. Click on Transform - Pivot Column. Select 'Date' as the 'Values Column'.
Go to the Region column. Click on Transform - Unpivot Column. Select 'Date' as the 'Values Column'.
Go to the Region column. Click on Transform - Unpivot Column. Select 'SalesVolume' as the 'Values Column'.
Go to the Region column. Click on Transform - Pivot Column. Select 'SalesVolume' as the 'Values Column'.
explanation: To pivot, select the Region column and use Transform > Pivot Column. The 'Values Column' should be SalesVolume (the field to aggregate). The unique values of Region become new column headers.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Profile and clean the data > Resolve inconsistencies, unexpected or null values
commonTrap: Thinking Fill Down only fills one blank cell, or fills the entire column with the top value
question: I have a column with values: Description, First Description, null, null, Second Description, null, null. I click on Transform - 'Fill Down'. What does it do and what is the final result?
choices: The entire column is overwritten by the top-most value. Result: Description, Description, Description, Description, Description, Description, Description.

A value in one cell gets copied down to fill in any blank (null) cells. Result: Description, First Description, First Description, First Description, Second Description, Second Description, Second Description.
A value in one cell gets copied down to only one blank cell underneath. Result: Description, First Description, First Description, null, Second Description, Second Description, null.
explanation: Fill Down replaces null values with the last non-null value above them. Each non-null value 'fills down' until the next non-null value. It does not overwrite existing non-null values.

transformationPreview.label: Fill Down — null cells inherit the last non-null value above
